title: Isolation-based Spherical Ensemble Representations for Tabular Anomaly Detection
summary: Unsupervised tabular anomaly detection must identify global, local, and dependency anomalies without labels while remaining scalable on heterogeneous tabular data. ISER builds t spherical ensemble representations by sampling ψ points, using nearest-neighbor hypersphere radii as a monotonic density proxy, and scores points via average or cosine similarity to an all-ones anomaly reference; ISER-IF applies Isolation Forest to the transformed representation space. On 20 benchmark datasets ISER-S reaches average AUC-ROC 0.8523, and on Ionosphere ISER-IF raises iForest AUC-ROC from 0.8530 to 0.9314.

match_target.why: User hint specifies Table IV, ISER-IF AUC-ROC on Ionosphere. It is a small dataset and directly demonstrates the central ISER-IF contribution: enhancing iForest through ISER ensemble representations.

tolerance.why: No std/CI is reported for the target. AUC-ROC is a bounded score printed in [0,1] on Ionosphere with 351 examples (<2000), so tolerance rule 3 gives 0.02 absolute points.

requirements.stmt: For each of t partitionings, randomly sample a subset of size ψ without replacement.
requirements.quote: we begin by randomly sampling a subset Di ⊂D of size ψ without replacement

requirements.stmt: For each sampled center z, define the hypersphere radius as the nearest-neighbor distance to another sampled point.
requirements.quote: When a hypersphere expands from a random point to its nearest neighbor, the radius reflects local crowding.

requirements.stmt: For a query point x, consider all covering hyperspheres and select the one with smallest radius.
requirements.quote: we select the covering hypersphere with the smallest radius:

requirements.stmt: Use radius as a monotonic density proxy: smaller radii produce smaller φ values.
requirements.quote: smaller radii (characteristic of denser regions) yield smaller φ values

requirements.stmt: If x is not covered by any hypersphere in a partitioning, assign φ_i(x)=1.
requirements.quote: When x is covered by no hypersphere in Hi, we assign φi(x) = 1

requirements.stmt: Construct the ensemble representation Φ(x) by concatenating φ_i(x) over all t partitionings.
requirements.quote: The ensemble representation of point x is constructed by concatenating the coverage indicators from all t partitionings:

requirements.stmt: ISER-A computes the anomaly score as the arithmetic mean of the ensemble representation.
requirements.quote: The average-based anomaly score is computed as the arithmetic mean of all ensemble components

requirements.stmt: ISER-S computes the anomaly score using cosine similarity between Φ(x) and the anomaly reference vector.
requirements.quote: cosine similarity between the point’s ensemble representation and the anomaly reference vector

requirements.stmt: The anomaly reference vector is the all-ones vector representing consistent isolation across partitionings.
requirements.quote: This vector represents the theoretical pattern of a point that lies outside all hyperspheres across all partitionings

requirements.stmt: ISER-IF applies iForest to the transformed ISER feature space Φ(x), not the original feature space.
requirements.quote: we apply iForest to the transformed feature space Φ(x).

requirements.stmt: ISER-IF modifies the iForest anomaly score to account for the inverted isolation behavior in Φ-space.
requirements.quote: To accommodate this inversion, we modify the original iForest anomaly scoring function

requirements.stmt: Evaluate anomaly detection performance with AUC-ROC.
requirements.quote: We use Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC-ROC) as evaluation metrics.

requirements.stmt: Repeat each experiment 5 times and report the average result.
requirements.quote: Each experiment is repeated 5 times and reported average results.

requirements.stmt: Use ψ from powers of two up to 256 and default t=200 for iForest/iNNE/IDK/ADERH/proposed methods.
requirements.quote: For iForest, iNNE, IDK, ADERH and proposed methods, ψ ∈ {2m, m = 1, 2, . . . , 8} and with default t = 200.

requirements.stmt: Use the unsupervised contaminated-dataset setting: fit and score all points, with labels only for evaluation.
requirements.quote: Following the unsupervised setting, our experiments assume access to the entire dataset containing both normal and anomalous instances during training
